h: Tips for a big-sky Essex garden day
p: Hyde Hall sits on a hilltop near the village of Rettendon, south-east of Chelmsford, and the views across the surrounding countryside are part of the appeal. On a clear day, you can see for miles across the Essex fields. The flip side is that it's exposed, so bring a hat and sun cream in summer and a warm layer when the wind picks up.

The garden has grown hugely over the years, with big new areas opening up beyond the original planting. That means there's lots to explore, from the formal Hilltop Garden near the old farmhouse to wilder meadows and new landscapes beyond. Allow two to three hours for a good look round, or longer if you're stopping for lunch.

The plant centre and shop are well worth a browse, especially if the Dry Garden has given you ideas for coping with a hot summer in your own patch. Keen gardeners should check the events calendar, as the RHS runs talks, workshops and seasonal events throughout the year.
Families are well catered for too, with space for kids to run around and seasonal trails to follow.

Afterwards, Chelmsford has plenty of shops and places to eat, and its compact cathedral is worth a peek. For a breath of sea air, head east to Maldon on the Blackwater estuary, famous for its salt and the old Thames sailing barges moored at the Hythe Quay. Danbury Country Park is another lovely nearby spot for a woodland walk.
